acceptedFindings.claim: Mathematics is a first-class formal-domain candidate, but its internal topology already contains domains, bridges and axes; root admission still requires explicit criteria.
Probability and Statistics are distinct identities; Statistics additionally functions as a cross-domain inferential/methodological axis.
Dynamical Systems, Systems Theory/Control and Systems Engineering are three distinct identities with specific bridge relations.
Geochemistry is a stable Earth↔chemistry bridge spanning planetary, atmospheric, hydrologic and biospheric contexts.
Physical Geography is a stable geography↔Earth/environment bridge and should not be collapsed into either generic Earth Science or human geography.
Genetics and Genomics are distinct but coupled identities; Genomics adds genome-scale technology, data and computation dimensions.

Information Science and Librarianship are overlapping but distinct: one centers inquiry into information organization/flow/use, the other includes professional/institutional information-access practice and infrastructure.

controls: Dynamical Systems != Systems Theory/Control != Systems Engineering.

splitRepairs.reason: MSC2020 has separate major classes 60-XX and 62-XX; relation is overlap/cross-reference, not identity.
MSC2020 separates 37-XX Dynamical systems and 93-XX Systems theory; control. Systems Engineering remains a third distinct identity.
NHGRI distinguishes genetics (genes/inheritance) from genomics (whole genomes and genome-scale inquiry).
ASIS&T supports a scientific/inquiry identity for Information Science while ALA supports a professional Library and Information Studies/Librarianship identity; overlap does not imply equivalence.
